children: Oil futures decline in Asia as traders weigh the risk of oversupply against continued attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. A recovery in crude exports is driving expectations of a global surplus but the balance is fragile. ANZ Research analysts say that despite some improvement in inventories and product availability over the past few weeks, the oil market is under severe strain. Global inventories remain extremely low and spare capacity to endure future supply disruptions is non-existent. "This leaves the market heavily exposed to further upside rallies amid the current geopolitical backdrop." Front-month WTI falls 0.6% to $81.53 a barrel; front-month Brent declines 0.6% to $90.89 a barrel.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
